title: The ASASSN-14ko AGN stayed steady when the period decrease stopped, so a disc-state change is excluded; star-disc drag fits only with orbital precession, a radiation-pressure disc and an evolved star
abstract: Question: the orbital period of the repeating nuclear transient ASASSN-14ko decreased fast before 2020 and then stayed constant (X-ray clock, 108.44 d in 2020-2024). Can drag in the gas disc of the host AGN explain this stall? Drag per crossing follows the disc surface density Sigma, so the stall needs either a fall of Sigma (a change of disc state) or a change of the crossing geometry by apsidal precession. Approach: we took single-marker timing sets from earlier campaign studies, measured the AGN in the two eras with 23 WISE/NEOWISE visits (2010-2024, field-star zero points), converted the luminosity change into allowed Sigma changes with a steady alpha-disc solver, computed the drag over a precession cycle for inclined eccentric orbits, and fitted a precessing drag clock to 34 timing points. Results: with the X-ray clock, the stall-era drag must be at most 0.16-0.76 of the earlier drag (95%); the Swift UVW2 peaks alone show no stall. The nucleus is AGN-dominated in W2 (W1-W2 = 1.13). Its W2 flux was 1.072 times higher in the stall era (95%: 1.036-1.109) and did not change across the transition. Thus Sigma changed by a factor 0.86-1.11 at most in gas-pressure, radiation-pressure and hot-flow discs, which excludes a disc-state change for all X-ray variants. Precession changes the drag by at most a factor 3.7 if Sigma decreases outward, but in a radiation-pressure inner disc (Sigma ~ r^1.5) the drag can reach zero. A precessing drag clock with such a disc fits the timing better than a two-break clock (Delta AIC = 2.9-3.7, two fewer parameters; a gas-pressure disc is worse) and predicts the SPHEREx peak of flare 37 within 1.2 d. Its precession rate (0.082-0.090 rad per orbit) puts the pericentre at about 105-180 gravitational radii, excludes black-hole masses of 1e8 Msun or more, and needs a subgiant or giant star (12-66 Rsun for 1e7-1e7.86 Msun). At the mid-infrared AGN luminosity this crossing radius is radiation-pressure dominated and has enough Sigma for alpha of 0.01-0.1. Forecasts: flare 41 near 2026-11-14 (two breaks: 2026-11-24), flare 42 near 2027-02-28 (2027-03-12). Limitations: we assume drag is the only cause; the stall depends on the timing marker; steady Shakura-Sunyaev discs, first-order precession and a thin-disc crossing model; uncertain AGN fraction and bolometric correction; few quiescent X-ray visits before 2020; a modest model preference that depends on the 2024-2026 flares; no public data cover the 2026 flares.

display.caption: Top: O-C of ASASSN-14ko flare markers against the constant 108.44 d X-ray clock; orange band: period-decrease era, blue band: stall era. Below: WISE W1/W2 visit fluxes of the AGN-dominated nucleus, quiescent Swift XRT 2-10 keV rates and quiescent ASAS-SN g fluxes. The AGN did not fade when the period decrease stopped.

Allowed stall-era/decrease-era change of the disc surface density from the measured AGN luminosity (green, four disc regimes) against the drag fraction that the timing needs (95% upper limits). They do not overlap for the X-ray clock, so a change of disc state cannot make the stall.

Top: O-C of optical peaks and X-ray ingress times with four fitted clocks. Bottom: model period against cycle. A drag clock in a precessing orbit that crosses a radiation-pressure disc reproduces the decrease, the stall and the renewed decrease.
